# Judith Chapter 8 — The LOGOS Bible (Formal)
**Translator:** LOGOS | **Source:** Codex Vaticanus, Judith 8 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/JDT_008_page_001.jpg

---

**8:1** In those days Judith came to hear of it — Judith, daughter of Merari son of Ox son of Joseph son of Oziel son of Elkiah son of Ananias son of Gideon son of Raphain son of Ahitub son of Elihu son of Eliab son of Nathanael son of Salamiel son of Sarasadai son of Israel.

**8:2** Her husband had been Manasseh, of her own tribe and family. He had died during the barley harvest.

**8:3** He was standing over the men who were binding sheaves in the field when the heat struck him on the head. He was carried to bed and died in his city of Bethulia, and was buried with his ancestors in the field between Dothan and Balamon.

**8:4** Judith had lived as a widow in her house for three years and four months.

**8:5** She had set up a tent for herself on the roof of her house, put on sackcloth around her waist, and worn widow's clothing.

**8:6** She fasted every day of her widowhood except the eves of the Sabbaths and the Sabbaths themselves, the eves of the new moons and the new moons, the festivals, and the days of rejoicing of the house of Israel.

**8:7** She was very beautiful in appearance and exceedingly lovely to look upon. Her husband Manasseh had left her gold and silver, male servants and female servants, livestock and fields; and she had remained the mistress of all these things.

**8:8** No one spoke an ill word about her, for she feared God exceedingly.

**8:9** Now she heard the harsh words the people were speaking against Uzziah their ruler, because they had lost heart over the lack of water. And Judith heard everything Uzziah said to them — how he had sworn to them that he would surrender the city to the Assyrians after five days.

**8:10** She sent her maidservant, who oversaw all her affairs, to summon Uzziah and Chabris and Charmis, the elders of her city.

**8:11** When they came to her she said to them: "Listen to me, rulers of the people of Bethulia! What you have said to the people today is not right — this oath you have sworn and made between God and yourselves, promising to hand over the city to our enemies unless within these days the Lord turns to help us.

**8:12** Who do you think you are, that you have put God to the test today and have set yourselves in God's place among human beings?

**8:13** Now you are putting the Lord Almighty to the test — yet you will never understand anything about him!

**8:14** For you cannot plumb the depths of the human heart or grasp the thoughts of the human mind — so how will you search out God, who made all these things, and know his mind and understand his purposes? No, brothers — do not anger the Lord our God.

**8:15** For if he chooses not to help us within these five days, he has the power to protect us within whatever days he pleases — or indeed to destroy us in full view of our enemies.

**8:16** Do not lay pledges against the purposes of the Lord our God, for God is not like a man, to be coerced by threats, nor like a human being, to be won over by pleading.

**8:17** Therefore let us wait for the salvation that comes from him and cry out to him to help us. If it pleases him, he will hear our voice.

**8:18** For there has not arisen in our generation, nor does there exist today, any tribe or family or people or city among us that worships gods made by human hands, as was the case in former days —

**8:19** on account of which our ancestors were given over to the sword and to plunder and fell with great ruin before their enemies.

**8:20** But we know no other God but him, and we hope therefore that he will not despise us or any of our race.

**8:21** For if we are taken captive, all Judea will be taken captive and our sanctuaries will be plundered and God will demand an accounting of their blood from us.

**8:22** The slaughter of our kindred, the captivity of the land, and the desolation of our heritage he will bring down on our heads among the nations wherever we are enslaved — and we will become an offense and a reproach in the eyes of those who enslave us.

**8:23** For our slavery will bring no goodwill; the Lord our God will turn it into dishonor.

**8:24** And so, brothers, let us give our kindred this proof — that their very lives depend upon us, and the sanctuary and the temple and the altar rest on our shoulders.

**8:25** Above all let us give thanks to the Lord our God, who is testing us even as he tested our ancestors.

**8:26** Remember what he did with Abraham, how he tested Isaac, and what became of Jacob in Syrian Mesopotamia while he was tending the flocks of Laban his mother's brother.

**8:27** For as he did not try them to destruction — though the fire was in their hearts, as it were — so he does not exact vengeance on us; rather his hand disciplines those who draw near to him, as a warning to them.

**8:28** Then Uzziah said to her: "Everything you have said comes from a right heart, and no one can find fault with your words.

**8:29** And indeed this is not the first day your wisdom has been known; from the beginning of your life all the people have recognized your understanding, for the disposition of your heart has always been good.

**8:30** But the people were in extreme thirst and they compelled us to do as we told them, and to bind ourselves with an oath we cannot now transgress.

**8:31** So pray for us, for you are a devout woman — and the Lord will send rain to fill our cisterns and we will faint no more."

**8:32** Judith said to them: "Hear me, and I will do a thing that will be remembered among the children of our people for all generations.

**8:33** You are to stand at the gate tonight, and I will go out with my maidservant. And within the days after which you said you would hand over the city to our enemies, the Lord will deliver Israel by my hand.

**8:34** But do not ask me what I am doing, for I will tell you nothing until the task is accomplished."

**8:35** Uzziah and the rulers said to her: "Go in peace, and may the Lord God go before you to take vengeance on our enemies."

**8:36** Then they turned back from the tent and went to their posts.
